prose: Hunterbrook Media found that Meta's Muse agent can be prompted to compile dossiers on Facebook and Instagram accounts belonging to vulnerable groups - undocumented immigrants, transgender teachers, poll workers, Iranian dissidents, and women who said they had ordered abortion pills in ban states - many of them private individuals with no public persona. The finding cuts against Meta's 'safe, secure, private' marketing of Muse (launched Sept. 8, 3.4M+ downloads, #1 free iPhone app): early scrutiny focused on how Muse handles its own users' data, but Hunterbrook tested what it does with other people's. Meta asked for more information and has not responded to repeated requests since. Hunterbrook Capital discloses no related positions.
highlights: Hunterbrook: Muse can be prompted to build dossiers on members of vulnerable groups
Groups named: undocumented immigrants, transgender teachers, poll workers, Iranian dissidents, women who ordered abortion pills in ban states
Many targeted accounts were private individuals with no public persona
Cuts against Meta's 'safe, secure, private' marketing of Muse
Muse launched Sept. 8 and has 3.4M+ downloads; #1 free iPhone app in the US
Meta asked for more information, then stopped responding to requests for comment
quotes: what the agent can do with other people's data
